text:
maria: FYI we saw ~40% of GPU nodes cordoned/drianed during the autoscaler rollout last night, caused a few model pods to restart and lost warm KV caches. Noticed some sidecars without the gpu toleration.

liam: ugh. which sidecars? any specific daemonsets?

maria: ml-metrics-exporter and an older logging sidecar on the k8s pool. They have no toleration for the gpu taint so autoscaler treated them as normal pods and kicked nodes for scale-down.

sneha: can we reproduce locally? we have a small cluster in staging to repro the drain behavior.

maria: yes reproduced in staging. sequence: 1) CA decides to scale down GPU node pool 2) node gets cordoned 3) pods with toleration missing evict immediately 4) some pods reschedule onto non-gpu nodes which breaks nodeSelector affinity and causes image pull delays.

infra-bot: Deploy job #4321 started by @maria: patching daemonset "ml-metrics-exporter" to add toleration.

liam: quick mitigation options: add toleration to the sidecars, or make those sidecars run as node-affinity: preferNoSchedule on gpu nodes, or mark the GPU nodes as protected with a specific taint that only infra-managed pods tolerate.

alex: adding toleration is fastest. suggested toleration YAML snippet:```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "redwood.com/gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```

jorge: we should avoid adding broad tolerations. maybe better to update the DaemonSet to use hostNetwork and run un-tolerated versions that are benign on CPU nodes? or move metrics sidecar into a central aggregator (single node) so it's not on GPU nodes at all.

sneha: for the logging sidecar we can't move it easily. But we can add a specific toleration, scoped to the image tag so we don't accidentally open it to other taints. Also add pod anti-affinity to avoid collocating critical pods with unrelated workloads.

maria: decision: patch the two daemonsets in prod with the explicit toleration (minimal scope), add a follow-up ticket to refactor logging sidecar to a central aggregator. I'll roll the toleration as a canary to one region first.

liam: also useful to add a quick admission webhook check that flags pods missing required tolerations when they have gpu nodeSelector or gpu affinity. can be a cheap safeguard.

alex: +1. We have a small validating webhook prototype in tools/infra-checks. I'll open a PR to extend it to check for cluster label "pool=gpu" and required toleration keys.

maria: patch applied in us-west-2 canary pool. Monitoring: token-cache hit rate dropping expected until pods warm back up. If no regressions in 30m will push global.

jorge: for long term: consider taint key naming convention and an operator to auto-insert tolerations for infra-managed daemonsets. reduces human error.

sneha: note on docs: add "GPU node lifecycle" section explaining: taint->toleration coupling, nodeSelector vs nodeAffinity, and how autoscaler interacts with DaemonSets.

liam: commands used during the patch:```bash
kubectl -n infra patch daemonset ml-metrics-exporter --type=json -p='[{
  "op": "add",
  "path": "/spec/template/spec/tolerations",
  "value": [{"key":"redwood.com/gpu","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]
}]'
```

maria: postmortem next week if anything leaks. For now watch for pods that end up on non-gpu nodes and for increased egress/latency. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
